source: AA HL 2021 May P2 TZ2 Q9 (no calculator needed). Binomial (1+t)^-1, Maclaurin series of sec x from cos x, limit of x arctan 2x / (sec x - 1) = 4.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write down the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (1 + t)^-1 in ascending powers of t.
parts.tolerance: Accept the three terms listed: 1, -t, t^2.

parts.label: b
parts.description: By using the Maclaurin series for cos x and the result from part (a), show that the Maclaurin series for sec x up to and including the term in x^4 is 1 + x^2/2 + 5x^4/24.
parts.tolerance: Condone the absence of '...'. The two method marks are implied by correct working.
parts.notes: (M1) for sec x = 1/(1 - x^2/2! + x^4/4! - ...). (M1) for t = cos x - 1 substituted into 1 - t + t^2. A1 for the correct substituted expression. A1 for both x^4 contributions, -x^4/24 and +x^4/4, seen before the given answer. AG. Differentiating sec x four times earns no marks: the question requires the method of (a) and (b).

parts.label: c
parts.description: By using the Maclaurin series for arctan x and the result from part (b), find the limit as x -> 0 of (x arctan 2x)/(sec x - 1).
parts.tolerance: Condone a missing 'lim' and errors in higher-order terms. Only the leading terms 2x^2 and x^2/2 are needed.
parts.notes: M1 for substituting arctan 2x = 2x - (2x)^3/3 + ... and the sec x series into the limit; do not award unless x is replaced by 2x in arctan. A1 for (2x^2 - 8x^4/3 + ...)/(x^2/2 + 5x^4/24) or after dividing by x^2. A1 for 4. L'Hopital's rule earns no marks: the question requires Maclaurin series.
parts.follow_through: Award the final A1 for the limit correctly obtained from the candidate's own leading coefficients.

source: AA HL 2021 Nov P1 Q10 (no calculator). Kinematics: v(t) = 4 + 4t - 3t^2 for 0 <= t <= 3, P at origin at t = 0. Max velocity at t = 2/3; displacement 88/27 m; sketch of v with t-intercept 2, start (0, 4), vertex (2/3, 16/3), end (3, -11); total distance 8 + 5 = 13 m.

parts.label: a.i
parts.description: A particle P moves along the x-axis with velocity v(t) = 4 + 4t - 3t^2 m/s for 0 <= t <= 3; at t = 0 it is at the origin O. Find the value of t when P reaches its maximum velocity.
parts.tolerance: Accept -b/(2a) = -4/(2(-3)) or the average of the roots (-2/3 + 2)/2.
parts.notes: (M1) for a valid approach to find the turning point, e.g. v'(t) = 4 - 6t = 0. A1 for t = 2/3. The official markscheme totals (a)(i) and (a)(ii) as [7]; this split (2 + 5) follows its mark lines.

parts.label: a.ii
parts.description: Show that the distance of P from O at this time is 88/27 metres.
parts.tolerance: Accept a definite integral from 0 to 2/3 in place of finding c.
parts.notes: (M1) for attempting to integrate v. A1 for 4t + 2t^2, A1 for -t^3. (M1) for substituting their t into their integral. A1 for 8/3 + 8/9 - 8/27 or an equivalent line seen before the given answer. AG.
parts.follow_through: The substitution (M1) follows through from the candidate's t in (a)(i).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Sketch a graph of v against t on the given axes, clearly showing any points of intersection with the axes.

expected.answer: Concave-down parabola from (0, 4), vertex near (2/3, 16/3), crossing the t-axis at t = 2, ending at t = 3 (v = -11).

parts.tolerance: The value v(3) = -11 need not be labelled, but the end of the domain at t = 3 must be clearly indicated. Vertex position is approximate.
parts.notes: (M1) for a valid approach to solve 4 + 4t - 3t^2 = 0, e.g. (2 - t)(2 + 3t) (may be seen in (a)). A1 for the t-intercept at t = 2. A1 for the domain 0 to 3 starting at (0, 4). A1 for the vertex at approximately t = 2/3 with v > 4. The last two A marks require a concave-down parabola; they are independent of each other and of the (M1). Drawing the curve outside 0 <= t <= 3 (e.g. to the root t = -2/3) loses the domain A1.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the total distance travelled by P.
parts.tolerance: Accept the integral of |v| from 0 to 3 as both method marks.
parts.notes: (M1) for recognising to integrate from 0 to 2 and from 2 to 3 (or the integral of |v|). A1 for 8. A1 for -5. (M1) for summing the magnitudes: int_0^2 v dt - int_2^3 v dt. A1 for 13. The integral from 0 to 3 (= 3) is the displacement, not the distance, and earns no marks on its own.
parts.follow_through: Award the A marks from the candidate's own antiderivative in (a)(ii) and root in (b).

source: AA HL 2021 May P1 TZ2 Q9 (no calculator). Integral of sin x cos x / (sin^2 x - sin x - 2) by substitution u = sin x, then partial fractions u/((u+1)(u-2)) = 1/(3(u+1)) + 2/(3(u-2)).

parts.label: a
parts.description: By using the substitution u = sin x, find the integral of (sin x cos x)/(sin^2 x - sin x - 2) dx.
parts.tolerance: Accept equivalent forms, e.g. (1/3) ln(1 + sin x) + (2/3) ln(2 - sin x) + C. Condone further simplification of the correct answer.
parts.notes: A1 for du = cos x dx. A1 for the integral of u/(u^2 - u - 2) du. M1 for attempting partial fractions. (M1) for a valid attempt to find A and B. A1 for A = 1/3 and B = 2/3. A1 for (1/3) ln|u + 1| + (2/3) ln|u - 2|; condone missing +C or moduli here. A1 for the final answer in x with +C and moduli (or equivalent). A final answer left in terms of u earns the first six marks only.
parts.follow_through: Award the two final A1 marks from the candidate's own A and B, provided both are non-zero.

source: AA HL 2021 Nov P1 Q8 (no calculator). Linear first-order DE dy/dx = ln(2x)/x^2 - 2y/x, y = 4 at x = 1/2. Integrating factor x^2; integration by parts of ln 2x; c = 3/2.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = ln(2x)/x^2 - 2y/x, x > 0, given that y = 4 at x = 1/2. Give the answer in the form y = f(x).
parts.tolerance: Accept equivalent forms, e.g. y = (2x ln 2x - 2x + 3)/(2x^2).
parts.notes: (M1) for rearranging to dy/dx + 2y/x = ln(2x)/x^2. (M1) for attempting the integrating factor. (A1) for x^2. (M1) for attempting integration by parts on the integral of ln 2x. A1 for x^2 y = x ln 2x - x (+c). M1 for substituting x = 1/2, y = 4 into an integrated equation involving c. A1 for the final answer. Not dividing c by x^2 loses the final A1. Treating the equation as separable earns no marks.
